idiomatic_translation.text: Too much or too little of the three that the medical texts reckon, beginning with wind, causes disease.

findings.issue: The Tamil appears to speak only of 'the three' reckoned by the authors of the treatises (நூலோர்), beginning with wind (வளி). Aiyar names them "humours" and calls the authors "sages". Both are interpretive expansions; 'sages' is broader than 'those learned in the texts'. "Go to either extreme" fairly renders 'whether they increase or decrease' (மிகினும் குறையினும்).

evidence.assessment: AI assessment: நூல் 'book, treatise'; வளி 'wind, air'. The Tamil does not appear to contain a word for 'humour'.

findings.issue: Endnote 35 was retrieved and read. It names the other two of the three as bile and phlegm. This is Aiyar's identification; the couplet names only wind. The draft does not list the other two.

findings.issue: A word in the Tamil and Aiyar's English may not correspond. The supplied Tamil reads அறவறிந்து, which as read would mean something like 'knowing fully'. Aiyar's "Eat with moderation" corresponds more naturally to a word meaning 'measure' (அளவு, giving அளவறிந்து, 'knowing the measure'). This may be an edition reading, a spelling convention or a transcription problem; it cannot be settled here and should be checked against the source page or a scan. The supplied text is preserved.
findings.proposed_correction: Do not change the Tamil. Check Kural 943 (and Kural 477) against the Wikisource revision and a scan of the printed edition, and record whether அறவறிந்து is the edition's reading.

idiomatic_translation.text: As well-being stays with one who knows to eat less, so disease stays with one who eats to excess.

findings.issue: The condition and its reward may have shifted. The Tamil appears to say that as pleasure or well-being (இன்பம்) stays with one who eats knowing to eat less (இழிவறிந்து), so disease stays with one who eats to great excess. Aiyar has "Health seeketh the man who eateth only when his stomach is empty": the condition becomes timing (an empty stomach) rather than moderation, and 'pleasure' becomes 'health'. Aiyar's contrast with eating to excess fits the moderation reading better.

input_quotes: Even as Health seeketh the man who eateth only when his stomach is empty
evidence.assessment: AI assessment: இழிவு ordinarily means lowness or lessening; இன்பம் 'pleasure, happiness'; நிற்கும் 'will stay'. Whether இழிவு here means eating less or an emptied stomach needs Tamil review.

findings.issue: "Seeketh" renders நிற்கும் ('stays, abides'), and Disease is personified like Health. The parallel structure is kept.
